problem: Audio-visual navigation agents reach ~98% success on heard sounds but drop to ~52% on unheard sounds, because simple convolutional audio encoders under-exploit spatial cues and fixed-weight audio-visual concatenation cannot adapt modality contributions.
motivation: Real deployments involve diverse sounds that training data cannot cover, so generalization across sound sources and scenes is essential. Audio implicitly carries spatial information (direction, distance, room structure), which could be used to guide fusion rather than being just another concatenated feature.
key_idea: Extract an audio spatial state with a CRNN plus intensity attention, and use it as the query in cross-attention over visual and audio features, with a learned gate, to fuse the modalities adaptively.
insight: Both components matter on unheard sounds. Ablation on Replica Unheard: SoundSpaces baseline SPL 34.7, w/o ASGF 38.8, w/o ASE (learnable query) 59.5, full 63.3. Removing ASGF hurts most, so guided fusion is the main gain, while ASE adds a further gain. t-SNE shows ASE features vary smoothly with target distance and azimuth. Caveat: gains come from a single fixed training setup and the paper gives no multi-seed variance.
method: Observation encoders: two CNNs encode depth/RGB visual features D_t and binaural spectrogram audio features A_t.
Audio Spatial State Encoder (ASE): STFT binaural spectrogram, then CNN keeping the time axis, then BiGRU giving frame-wise 512-d embeddings.
Audio intensity attention: per-frame intensity is the mean magnitude over frequency and channel, softmax over time gives weights, and the weighted sum of embeddings gives the audio spatial state e_t.
ASGF cross-attention: LN and projection of visual and audio features are concatenated as keys/values, and e_t is the query, giving context c_t; a residual gives c_t + e_t.
Adaptive gate: alpha_t = sigmoid(MLP(LN(e_t))) blends the attended state and e_t, h_t = LN(alpha*h_hat + (1-alpha)*e_t).
Policy: fused features go through a GRU for temporal context, then an Actor-Critic head trained with RL (built on the SoundSpaces codebase).

setting.backbone: CNN encoders + BiGRU ASE + cross-attention fusion + GRU + Actor-Critic (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces episodes on Replica and Matterport3D; heard setting uses a telephone sound, unheard uses different sounds at test; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + binaural spectrogram audio
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward, turn left, turn right, stop

numbers_note: The paper does not name the official split; test on unseen scenes is assumed. Baselines' numbers were omitted. Ablation variants (w/o ASGF, w/o ASE) exist in Table 2 for the Unheard task only.
results: On unheard sounds, ASGF-Nav reaches Replica SPL 63.3 / SR 76.5 / SNA 36.9 and Matterport3D SPL 52.2 / SR 66.4 / SNA 29.9, well above AV-WAN (Replica 34.7/52.8/27.1; MP3D 40.9/56.7/30.6) and AGSA. On heard sounds it is competitive but below AV-WAN (Replica SR 94.5 vs 98.7; MP3D SR 87.6 vs 93.6).
limitations: Heard-sound performance is lower than AV-WAN, particularly on Matterport3D, and the SNA on MP3D Unheard is slightly below AV-WAN's.
Evaluated only in simulation on two datasets with a single training-sound setup; no real robot, no variance across seeds.
Text claims the improvement figures as percentages (28.6%, 23.7%, 9.8%) without clear baseline definition.
